summary: The run is interpretable per shape (only unpooler decode_16/32 can move and the profile gives the Triton kernel's own us, hence its TB/s), but the parent's result already answers the stated question against it: the same plain Triton full-K stream on the same 67 MB took 20.2 us at BLOCK_M=16 (3.3 TB/s) and 25.2 us at BLOCK_M=32 (2.7 TB/s), against nvjet's 18.4/18.8 us single kernel here, so the likely outcome is flat-to-loss at m=16 and a large loss at m=32; one control that isolates the BLOCK_M=32 tile is needed to read a mixed result.
justification: Mechanism: unpooler at m=16/32 is a 67.1 MB bf16 stream (n=8192, k=4096), floor 14.1 us; master runs one non-splitK nvjet 2x1 kernel at 18.4 us (m=16) / 18.8 us (m=32) with reported medians 18.3-18.9 us (BEST job 9aa98e889be140eb profile), i.e. ~3.6 TB/s with no reduce node and no inter-node gap to remove. A gain therefore needs the Triton kernel itself to beat 18.4 us (>= 3.65 TB/s), and the 'target <= 17 us' in expected needs 3.95 TB/s. The only measurement of this kernel family in the workspace is the parent pooler-triton-skinny-m32 (done/neutral, 0.998x): _pooler_skinny_kernel on the same 67 MB (BLOCK_N=32, BLOCK_K=256, 4 stages, 32 K-steps) ran 20.2 us at m=1/8/16 and 25.2 us at m=32. Its 5-6% pooler gains at m<=16 came entirely from dropping the 1.6-1.9 us splitKreduce plus the graph gap (cuBLAS kernel sum 19.9-20.6 us vs reported 21.2-21.9); the Triton stream was slower than nvjet's own kernel time. Unpooler has nothing to drop, so the parent's data predict ~20 us vs 18.4 (loss ~8%) at m=16 and ~25 us vs 18.8 (loss ~25%) at m=32 unless BLOCK_N=64 / 16 K-steps changes the bandwidth picture, which the hypothesis asserts but does not argue (2x the weight bytes in flight per SM is the one real difference; fewer K-steps amortise the pipeline prologue worse, not better). The hypothesis was written before the parent's result and does not mention the m=32 anomaly at all. Shape/weight consistency with TASK.md is fine: both target shapes weigh 62, unpooler is ~31% of decode_16 and ~30% of decode_32, so a full success (18.6 -> 17 us) is ~+2.7% on two of six loads, ~+0.9% geomean, under the +-1.5% CI, so the per-shape rows and the kernel us are the readout, never the headline. Weakest link: the stated question ('does the full-K Triton stream beat nvjet's 2x1 kernel') has already been answered negatively for this kernel at BLOCK_N=32 by the parent, and the parent's own Risk section says the dependents should be retuned (BLOCK_N=16/256 programs or num_stages=6) before running if the Triton kernel is not faster than nvjet; this spec changes BLOCK_N in the other direction (64) and keeps BLOCK_M=32 at m=32, the tile that lost 16% on pooler. Second concern: smem at BLOCK_M=32 is 4 stages x (64x256x2 + 32x256x2) = 192 KB, near the 227 KB limit; Triton may fail to pipeline at 4 stages, and raising to 6 as the Risk section suggests is impossible at that tile.
confounders: sglang-gemm-dispatch-parity (landed): inert on unpooler m=16/32; _bf16_gemm_dispatch_impl(x, W[:8192], None) resolves to the same nvjet_sm90_tst_64x16/64x32_64x16_2x1_v_bz_TNT the starter picked (unpooler rows flat in its attribution); this change replaces that call on exactly these two shapes and would behave identically with the parent absent.

router-hilo-at-m8 (landed): a different layer timed in its own CUDA graph, no shared kernel, memory or numerics; cannot confound the unpooler rows. It does affect the headline: because depends_on=pooler-triton-skinny-m32 is unpromoted, churn.py will build on the pooler branch's impl_commit d2840d0 (parity base e64f27e, ROUTER_FP32_MAX_TOKENS=8), so this run's aggregate lacks the +2.2% router gain and is not comparable to BEST 1.0307x; the per-shape attribution against the pooler result (same base blob 2752a01) is still correct.

pooler-triton-skinny-m32 (parent branch, unpromoted): shares the @triton.jit kernel; a BLOCK_N=64 specialization is a separate binary and pooler shapes are separate graphs, so no runtime interaction, but the inherited pooler decode_32 loss (0.887x, 24.5 vs 21.9 us) drags the headline and must be attributed away by comparing against the parent's result rows, not SGLang.
interference: A clean gain (both unpooler rows faster, kernel us < 18.4/18.8) would be unambiguous: nothing else in those graphs changes. A clean loss would be interpretable only at the family level if the kernel us lands near the parent's 3.3 TB/s. The most likely outcome on the parent's evidence is mixed: m=16 near-flat or a small loss and m=32 a large loss, and that m=32 row is ambiguous between (a) the BLOCK_M=32 tl.dot tile / 192 KB smem pipeline being pathological, as the pooler m=32 row (25.2 vs 20.2 us for identical bytes) already suggests, and (b) the Triton stream's bandwidth ceiling. A 'control' that holds everything else and runs BLOCK_M=16 for every m (two 16-row x tiles and two tl.dot per K-step against the one weight tile at m=32, weight still read once) separates the tile effect from the bandwidth effect, and also tells the o- and qkv-gate-triton-skinny siblings whether their m=32 rows are salvageable. ab-revert is not applicable: neither landed hypothesis touches the unpooler path, and reverting router-hilo-at-m8 is moot since the build base lacks it anyway. ab-tune: the parent's pooler tile has no effect on unpooler rows. One companion, priority 3; a second (BLOCK_N=32 / 256 programs for memory-level parallelism) is a retune to queue only after the kernel us is known, not a disambiguator.
rules_flags: No rule break found: bf16 x bf16 tl.dot with fp32 accumulation and one bf16 rounding at the store matches cuBLAS; the weight is read as stored (no repack, no precision change); the only allocation is a fixed-shape torch.empty from cfg; guard must branch on cfg m/n/k and x.shape/dtype/stride only (never values); no syncs, no caching of anything derived from data; prepare() warm-up must use synthetic zeros and discard outputs as the parent does.

Guard precision: route only when layer=='unpooler', 8 < cfg['m'] <= 32, cfg['n']==8192 and cfg['k']==4096, so the m=5 (n=1024 slice) and m=130/m=1000 outlier tests stay on cuBLAS; do not key on x.shape[0] alone since the slice at m<=8 has n=1024.

Compile/graph risk, not a rules risk: 4 stages at BLOCK_M=32/BLOCK_N=64/BLOCK_K=256 is 192 KB smem; if Triton silently drops stages or fails, the warm-up in prepare() must surface it before capture (warm every m in 9..32 as the parent does for 1..32).

companions.change: From the parent's branch (unpooler-full-triton-skinny-m32), keep the unpooler routing, grid (8192/64 = 128 programs), BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=256, num_stages=4, num_warps=4, fp32 accumulate and the bf16 store exactly as the parent, and change only the M tiling: BLOCK_M is 16 for every m in 9..32. For m > 16 the kernel keeps two fp32 accumulators [16, 64] and per K-step loads the one [64, 256] weight tile once and two [16, 256] x tiles (rows 0..15 and 16..31, rows >= m masked to zero), doing two tl.dot(x_i, tl.trans(w_tile), acc_i); for m <= 16 it is the parent's single-tile path (so unpooler decode_16 is byte-for-byte the parent's kernel and serves as the within-run control). Smem per stage drops to 32 KB weight + 2 x 8 KB x = 48 KB, 192 KB at 4 stages (same as the parent at m=32; if the parent had to drop to 3 stages, this one may keep 4). Two stores, one per 16-row accumulator, masked on rows < m. Warm m in 9..32 in prepare() on synthetic zeros. Pooler and every other layer unchanged from the parent.

expected.why: than the parent's m=32 row if the pooler's 25.2-vs-20.2 us m=32 penalty is the BLOCK_M=32 tl.dot tile; equal to the parent's row if it is bandwidth
identical kernel binary to the parent at m<=16; within-run control
m=8 slice and m>=128 stay on cuBLAS

companions.reason: Separates the m=32 row's result into tile (BLOCK_M=32 wgmma tile / smem pipeline) versus streaming bandwidth: if the parent loses at m=32 and this control does not, the family's m=32 problem is the 32-row tile and o-/qkv-gate-triton-skinny should adopt BLOCK_M=16 everywhere; if both lose equally, the plain Triton stream's ceiling (~3.3 TB/s on the pooler) is confirmed on a second shape and the whole skinny-Triton family should be withdrawn.

open_questions: The hypothesis predates the parent's result and should be read against it: on the same 67 MB the Triton stream took 20.2 us (m<=16) and 25.2 us (m=32) where nvjet's unpooler kernel takes 18.4/18.8 us; the implementer should state in the attempt file what BLOCK_N=64 / 16 K-steps is expected to change about that before spending the run, or apply the parent's own Risk-section retune (256 programs or more stages) inside this hypothesis's envelope.

Build base: churn.py will base this on the parent's impl_commit d2840d0 (no router-hilo-at-m8, ROUTER_FP32_MAX_TOKENS=8) because the parent is unpromoted; the headline cannot be compared to BEST and promotion of a gain would need a rebase onto master plus a fresh run. Consider whether the dispatcher should instead base on master and copy the kernel in (depends_on null), since the unpooler path shares no runtime state with the pooler path.

Smem budget at BLOCK_M=32: 4 x (32 KB + 16 KB) = 192 KB; confirm from the run log that Triton kept 4 stages (and did not fail to compile); 'raise num_stages to 6' in the Risk section is not possible at this tile.

Harvest criterion: the headline will straddle 1.0 even on success (~+0.9% geomean ceiling for 2 of 30 shapes) and is further depressed by the inherited pooler decode_32 loss; judge on the unpooler decode_16/32 rows versus the parent's result rows (18.71 / 18.63 us) and record 67.1 MB / kernel us in FINDINGS as the second datapoint on the plain-Triton streaming ceiling.

If the kernel us is below nvjet's 18.4/18.8 but the reported median is not, the loss is Triton launch-path overhead inside the graph, not bandwidth; separate those two readings before withdrawing the o- and qkv-gate siblings.
